note: Programs for farmers and ranchers with disabilities. Links were checked on the date shown; where verified is false the page could not be fetched by our checker and the program was confirmed from search results instead.

programs.name: USDA AgrAbility (NIFA)
programs.who: Farmers, ranchers, farm workers and family members in the US who have a disability or health condition.
programs.line: A USDA-funded program that pairs state Extension offices with disability groups to help you keep farming, at no cost to eligible farmers.
programs.note: Confirmed on the NIFA page via search results; contact SM.AgrAbility@usda.gov.

programs.name: National AgrAbility Project
programs.who: Farmers and ranchers with disabilities anywhere in the US, and the state projects that serve them.
programs.line: Run by Purdue University; finds the AgrAbility project for your state and has guides on tools, farm tasks and funding.
programs.note: Site's TLS chain didn't verify from our checker; confirmed via search results.

programs.name: California AgrAbility (UC Davis)
programs.who: California farmers, ranchers and farm workers with a disability or injury.
programs.line: California's state AgrAbility project: consultations, farm site assessments and safety evaluations. It does not pay for equipment itself.
programs.note: Page confirmed via search results only (UC Davis Biological and Agricultural Engineering).

programs.name: WorkBC Assistive Technology Services
programs.who: People in British Columbia, including self-employed people, whose disability or functional limit is a barrier to work.
programs.line: Run by the Neil Squire Society; funds work devices, equipment, workplace changes and vehicle modifications. Phone 1-844-453-5506.
programs.note: neilsquire.ca refuses automated fetches (403); confirmed via search results. Confirm current coverage at workbc-ats.ca.

gaps: The Canadian Agricultural Safety Association (casa-acsa.ca) was checked and has no disability-specific farm program, so it is not listed.
No USDA Farm Service Agency page for producers with disabilities was found; AgrAbility's financing FAQ points people to local FSA offices for loans.
